content.title: About
content.content: Mustard greens (Brassica juncea) are edible young leaves and stems of the plant, widely used in Asian cuisine. They have a mildly bitter, peppery flavor and a crunchy texture. Raw greens are often added to salads, smoothies, and as a side dish.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Mustard greens belong to the cruciferous family, along with broccoli, cabbage, and turnip.
In traditional Chinese medicine they are used to aid digestion.
High levels of glucosinolates give the leaves their distinctive sharp aroma.
In Japan, mustard greens are frequently pickled in soy sauce and rice vinegar.
Raw leaves are a rich source of vitamin K, important for blood clotting.

items.title: Rich in vitamin K
items.content: Vitamin K is essential for normal blood clotting and bone health.

items.title: Contains vitamins A and C
items.content: These vitamins support vision, immunity, and antioxidant protection.

items.title: Source of folate
items.content: Folate is important for DNA synthesis and especially beneficial during pregnancy.

items.title: Low‑calorie source of fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion and promotes a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Contains glucosinolates
items.content: These compounds may have anti‑cancer effects by stimulating cellular detoxification.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to cruciferous vegetables.

items.title: High glucosinolate content
items.content: Excessive intake can irritate the gastrointestinal tract.

items.title: Interaction with anticoagulants
items.content: High vitamin K levels may reduce the effectiveness of blood‑thinning medications.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Mustard greens can be eaten raw in salads, blended into smoothies, used as a garnish, or quickly sautéed with garlic and olive oil.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the greens in an airtight container in the refrigerator, where they stay fresh for 3–5 days. For longer storage, they can be frozen after blanching for 1–2 minutes.
